g1.label: 1 — appear on a national ___
g1.why: A story appears on a website — a page on the internet.

g2.label: 2 — facts from social media are ___
g2.why: Facts cannot be "careful"; the point is that they can cause harm.

g3.label: 3 — a different ___
g3.why: A caption is the text printed under a photo.

g4.label: 4 — two independent ___
g4.why: A source is where information comes from; sauces are for food.

g5.label: 5 — readers often ___ the story
g5.why: The prefix mis- means wrongly: they understand the story wrongly.

g6.label: 6 — articles they have never ___
g6.why: You open an article before you read it — that is what they skip.

g7.label: 7 — nineteenth-century papers ___ too
g7.why: To exaggerate is to make something sound bigger than it was.

g8.label: 8 — before anybody can ___ it
g8.why: To correct a story is to put the mistake right.

g1.label: 1 — the reporter ___ the story
g1.why: The reporter does the writing, so the active -ing participle is used.

g2.label: 2 — a story ___ by two sources
g2.why: The story receives the action ("by two sources"), so the -ed participle is used.

g3.label: 3 — the students ___ in the library
g3.why: The students are doing the sitting themselves: -ing.

g4.label: 4 — photos ___ on social media
g4.why: Somebody posts the photos, so the photos take the passive -ed participle.

g5.label: 5 — the journalist ___ from Delhi
g5.why: The journalist does the reporting: active -ing.

g6.label: 6 — a headline ___ in a hurry
g6.why: The headline is written by somebody, so use the past participle.

g7.label: 7 — anybody ___ for a second source
g7.why: "Anybody looking for..." = anybody who looks for: active -ing.

g8.label: 8 — the documentary ___ last year
g8.why: The documentary was made by somebody: past participle.

g1.label: 1 — the man ___ at the door
g1.why: "who is standing" shortens to "standing" — drop the relative pronoun and the form of be.

g2.label: 2 — the article ___ yesterday
g2.why: "which was published" shortens to the past participle "published".

g3.label: 3 — people ___ only one source
g3.why: "who use" becomes the -ing participle "using" because the people do the action.

g4.label: 4 — the photo ___ in 2019
g4.why: "that was taken" shortens to "taken" — the photo receives the action.

g5.label: 5 — the editor said they ___ every fact (reported speech)
g5.why: After a past reporting verb the present perfect or past goes one step back — from the Great Barrier Reef unit.

g6.label: 6 — if people ___ the whole article (2nd conditional)
g6.why: The second conditional is if + simple past with "would" in the other half — from the Canada conditionals unit.

g7.label: 7 — ___ where the picture came from
g7.why: The editor does the not-knowing, so the active participle starts the clause.

g8.label: 8 — ___ by millions of people
g8.why: The video receives the watching, so the past participle opens the clause.
